chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Segregation in Missouri and Kansas schools; Reno Club
summary: Kansas schools were integrated apart from Kansas City, Kansas, while Missouri clubs kept the races apart.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Yeah, the kids--all those schools have become segregated. They said it was a political move, but anyway the schools in Kansas City, Kansas was segregated. All the rest of the schools in Missouri and Kansas were integrated, you know, and very peaceful living there.
They were integrated way back then?
However, they always found they had trouble near the Missouri borderline, with the Arkansas border-
line, where agitators was comin' across, you know, and like that. But generally speaking you had no trouble at all--we lived very peaceful there, you know.
That was a good thing, wasn't it?

Yeah. I knew guys, if I might say --you know, you couldn't even sit with the white people over on the Missouri side; you had to go back in that little cub-byhole somewhere. You didn't mingle with your (inaudible).
Oh, isn't that interesting--I don't think anybody's ever brought this out, you see. Everybody thinks Missouri's so wide open and great.
But there was a snag to it?

Yeah, and you couldn't sit with them unless the boss really just went on and bent over backwards and said, "Come over here and talk," you know, something like that. Now, like the Reno Club, they would go get Basie or Joe Jones or somebody and come on, bring 'em over to the table and sit with them and talk.
And things, places like that where we had the spook breakfast, where they'd let 'em all get together. But now I'm superseding myself again.
Right, you're still back in college?
